Conditions of contradiction
1. Subject. If the subjects differ, there is no contradiction: “Knowledge is beneficial”; “Ignorance is not beneficial.”
2. Predicate. If the predicates differ, there is no contradiction: “Knowledge is beneficial”; “Knowledge is not harmful.”
3. Time. There is no contradiction between “The sun is shining,” meaning during the day, and “The sun is not shining,” meaning during the night.
4. Place. There is no contradiction between “The land is fertile,” meaning in the cultivated countryside, and “The land is not fertile,” meaning in the desert.

5. Potentiality and actuality. The two propositions must agree in potentiality and actuality. There is no contradiction between “Muḥammad is dead,” meaning potentially, and “Muḥammad is not dead,” mea…
6. Whole and part. There is no contradiction between “Iraq is fertile,” meaning part of it, and “Iraq is not fertile,” meaning the whole of it.

7. Condition. There is no contradiction between “The student will pass at the end of the year,” meaning if he works diligently, and “The student will not pass,” meaning if he does not work diligently.
8. Relation. There is no contradiction between “Four is a half,” meaning in relation to eight, and “Four is not a half,” meaning in relation to ten.
